issues.legal_issue: A measure authorizing cancellation of leases made in anticipation of intermediary abolition is protected when it is ancillary to carrying out the abolition of intermediary estates.
material_facts: The challenged enactment provided for acquisition of intermediary estates and authorized cancellation of certain leases made after legislation was contemplated if the Collector found they were outside the normal course of management and made in anticipation of abolition.
The Court considered such leases designed to extract value before transfer to the State to be a fraud on the enactment, and treated the cancellation power as ancillary to its purpose.
issues.conclusion: The lease-cancellation provision was an integral, ancillary part of the estate-acquisition enactment and was protected by Article 31-A(1)(a).
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A(1)(a) protects a provision that is ancillary to and serves the purposes of legislation for acquisition of an estate or rights in an estate. The legislature may also enact retrospective provisions, including provisions for setting aside instruments in appropriate circumstances; the Court referred by analogy to insolvency laws that permit certain transfers to be set aside. It also noted legislative competence over land under List II, Entry 18.

rule.if: constitutional_validity_challenge and intermediary_estate_acquisition_scheme and leases_made_in_anticipation_of_reform and leases_outside_normal_management

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A party challenges the constitutional validity of an enactment in a proceeding before the court.
predicates.intermediary_estate_acquisition_scheme: The enactment provides for acquisition of estates held by intermediaries as part of a reform abolishing intermediary interests.
predicates.leases_made_in_anticipation_of_reform: An intermediary made leases in anticipation of legislation abolishing intermediary interests.
predicates.leases_outside_normal_management: The leases were found to have been made outside the normal course of management, to secure value before the estate was transferred.

issues.definition: When a constitutional validity challenge concerns an intermediary-estate acquisition scheme and the disputed leases were made in anticipation of reform outside normal management, the lease-cancellation measure is protected as an ancillary measure.

issues.legal_issue: A rent limit for land allotted to former intermediaries is protected when it supports personal cultivation and prevents the creation of new intermediary relationships.
material_facts: The enactment allotted some land to former intermediaries for personal cultivation, with recipients holding it directly from the Government and paying revenue.
Some recipients were permitted to let their allotted land, while others generally could not do so except in specified circumstances.
The challenged rent limit restricted rent to a maximum of one and a half times the land revenue, reducing the incentive to let land rather than cultivate it personally.
issues.conclusion: The rent limit was an ancillary provision necessary to carry out the enactment's objectives and was protected by Article 31-A(1)(a).
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-A(1)(a) protects provisions ancillary to legislation for acquisition of estates or rights in estates when they serve the legislation's objectives. The Court relied on the enactment's scheme for allotting land for personal cultivation and its provisions governing allotment, the status of recipients, their relationship with Government, and their ability to let land (sections 29, 30, 32 and 37).

rule.if: constitutional_validity_challenge and intermediary_estate_reform_scheme and allotted_land_intended_for_personal_cultivation and letting_could_recreate_intermediation and rent_limit_discourages_letting

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A party challenges the constitutional validity of an enactment in a proceeding before the court.
predicates.intermediary_estate_reform_scheme: The enactment acquires intermediary estates and provides for allotting some land to former intermediaries.
predicates.allotted_land_intended_for_personal_cult: The enactment's scheme expects former intermediaries who receive land to cultivate it personally.
predicates.letting_could_recreate_intermediation: Permitting recipients to let their land without constraint could allow them to become a new kind of intermediary.
predicates.rent_limit_discourages_letting: A limit on rent reduces the financial incentive for recipients to let land instead of cultivating it personally.

issues.definition: When an intermediary-estate reform scheme allots land for personal cultivation, letting could recreate intermediation, and a rent limit discourages letting, the rent limit is protected as an ancillary measure.

issues.legal_issue: A state legislature may enact an estate-acquisition law for state purposes even if the acquired property may vest in the Union after acquisition.
material_facts: The Ajmer legislature enacted a law acquiring estates within Ajmer for the purposes of the State.
The challengers argued that the property would vest in the President and therefore the acquisition was for Union purposes.
The Court held that the purpose for which property was acquired, not the identity of the post-acquisition holder, determined legislative competence; the acquired estates later went to Rajasthan.
issues.conclusion: The enactment was within the Ajmer legislature's competence under List II, Entry 36.
issues.legal_principle: Under the pre-Seventh Amendment distribution of legislative powers, List I, Entry 33 concerned acquisition or requisition of property for Union purposes, while List II, Entry 36 concerned acquisition or requisition other than for Union purposes, subject to List III, Entry 42. The test is the purpose of the acquisition, not where title vests after acquisition. Section 21 of the Government of Part C States Act, 1951 empowered the Ajmer Legislative Assembly to legislate on matters in List II and List III.

predicates.legislative_competence_challenge: A party challenges whether a state legislature had authority to enact an acquisition law.
predicates.acquisition_law_enacted_by_state_legisla: A state legislature enacted a law providing for acquisition of property.
predicates.acquisition_for_state_purposes: The property was acquired for the purposes of the state rather than for Union purposes.

issues.definition: When a state legislature's authority to enact an acquisition law is challenged, it is competent to enact the law if the acquisition is for state purposes.

issues.legal_issue: A jagirdar's interest in an estate is not divisible into a revenue-assignment interest and a separate landholding interest when the grant conferred the estate and the revenue remission explains the assignment description.
material_facts: The claimant held a jagir under grants made before the relevant land-revenue regulation, and the grants described the jagirs as estates.
The land revenue on the grants had been remitted, leading to the holder being described as an assignee of land revenue.
The claimant also held land in the jagir, including uncultivated land, and the enactment defined intermediaries to include holders of estates and jagirdars.
issues.conclusion: The jagirdar was the holder of the jagir estate, and the State could take over the entire interest in that estate under the enactment.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(v), 2(viii) and 4 of the acquisition enactment, an intermediary included a holder of an estate and a jagirdar, and the intermediary's estate vested in the State. The Court considered the definition of jagirdar in section 2(15) of the Ajmer Tenancy and Land Records Act, 1950, and the Ajmer Land and Revenue Regulation, including sections 61 and 64 and section 2(d). It relied on Thakur Amarsinghji v. State of Rajasthan for the history and meaning of jagir grants, noting that the term encompassed grants conferring rights in respect of land revenue.

predicates.challenge_to_application_of_estate_acqui: A jagirdar challenges the application of an estate-acquisition law to the jagir.
predicates.law_covers_intermediary_estates: The acquisition law covers estates held by intermediaries, including jagirdars.
predicates.jagir_grant_conferred_estate_proprietors: The grant underlying the jagir conferred the estate on its holder, including rights in the land.
predicates.revenue_assignment_description_arose_fro: The holder was described as an assignee of land revenue because revenue on the granted estate had been remitted.

issues.definition: When an acquisition law covers intermediary estates and the jagir grant conferred the estate, with the revenue-assignment description resulting from revenue remission, the entire jagir estate interest is subject to resumption.
